transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I'm here because I feel like I lose control around food at night and just keep eating even when I tell myself to stop. It's gotten to the point where I feel really overwhelmed by it, and I don't know how to make it stop.
After these episodes of overeating, do you ever try to make up for it by vomiting, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?
No, I don't do any of those things. I've never tried to make myself throw up, use laxatives, or force myself to fast or over-exercise afterward.
Have you also been intentionally restricting your food intake during the day or trying to lose weight, or do these night eating episodes happen without any dieting or weight-loss efforts?

Yes, my cardiologist ordered me to restrict my portions and eat healthier to control my weight and blood pressure. I try really hard to follow those strict limits during the day, but that pressure seems to backfire and triggers these uncontrollable episodes at night when I'm alone.
Do these nighttime eating episodes happen mainly after you have been trying to diet or restrict your food during the day, or do they also happen when you are not restricting at all?

They almost always happen on the days when I've been trying hard to restrict my food. Ever since my cardiologist told me to limit my portions, trying to follow those strict rules during the day just builds up a lot of tension, which seems to trigger me losing control at night.
Do these nighttime overeating episodes also happen on days when you are not trying to restrict your eating or diet during the day, or only after you have been dieting/strictly limiting food?

I'm not entirely sure, and I haven't really thought about it in terms of my day-to-day dieting. To be honest, these episodes seem much more closely tied to my stress about my heart health and the nights when I'm left alone with my thoughts.

Do these nighttime eating episodes happen even on days when you are not trying to restrict your food intake or diet during the day, or do they mainly occur after periods of strict dieting or self-imposed food limits?

I'm not entirely sure about the connection to my daytime dieting specifically. However, I do know that this whole pattern of late-night eating definitely started right after my cardiologist told me to restrict my food intake.

Do you still have these nighttime eating episodes even on days when you are not trying to restrict your food intake during the day, or do they mainly happen after you’ve been dieting or limiting yourself?

I'm not quite sure and haven't really thought about it that way. Ever since my cardiologist's orders, I feel like I am constantly trying to restrict myself and watch what I eat every single day. Because of that, there aren't really any days where I'm not trying to limit my food.
Do you ever have these night eating episodes on days when you are not trying to restrict your food intake during the day, or do they only happen after you’ve been limiting yourself?
I'm really not sure, and I haven't thought about it in that way. I just know that the constant pressure to restrict what I eat makes the urges to eat at night much worse.
When the nighttime eating happens, is it mainly a reaction to feeling deprived from restricting during the day, or does it also happen on days when you have not been trying to limit your food intake?

I'm not sure how to break it down that way, as I've generally been trying to follow my doctor's strict diet rules overall. The nighttime eating seems more directly triggered by the stress of my medical appointments, worrying about my heart, or just being alone and restless at night. It doesn't really seem to depend on whether I restricted my food earlier that specific day.
Do these nighttime eating episodes happen even on days when you are not trying to restrict your food intake during the day, or are they mainly a result of feeling deprived after dieting?

While this pattern started after my cardiologist told me to restrict my diet, these episodes aren't really triggered by physical hunger or feeling starved from dieting. I do try to eat healthy during the day, but the nighttime eating is driven by stress, worrying about my heart, and feeling restless and alone. It is more about my anxiety than what I ate earlier in the day.

When you wake up at night and start eating, is it usually because you feel physically hungry or deprived from not eating enough during the day, or does it happen more from stress, anxiety, or being awake and restless?

It is definitely not out of physical hunger, as I have almost always already eaten dinner. Instead, it happens when I am up late working on my home-maintenance handbook, feeling restless, or worrying about my heart health after my medical appointments.
Do you ever wake up from sleep and eat without being fully aware of it, or are these eating episodes happening while you are awake and conscious at night?

I am completely awake and conscious during these episodes, which usually happen while I'm up late editing my handbook, worrying about my health, or waiting for my wife to go to bed. I am fully aware of what I'm doing—I can even hear myself telling myself "Alejandro, basta" to stop—but I just feel completely unable to control the urge to keep eating.

Have you ever had periods of eating a lot during the day or night that were not related to trying to restrict your food, or is the eating mainly a response to stress and the limits you place on yourself?

No, this out-of-control eating is actually quite new to me and is closely tied to the stress of my heart issues and the dietary restrictions from my cardiologist about four months ago. Before I was told to restrict my food and started worrying about my heart, I never experienced these episodes of losing control and eating huge amounts at night.

Before your cardiologist told you to restrict your food, did you ever have episodes of eating a lot with a sense of loss of control, or did this only start after you began trying to limit your intake?

No, I never had these issues before. This pattern of losing control and overeating only started about four months ago, right after my cardiologist told me to restrict my food and limit my portions. Before that, I never had these late-night episodes where I felt so out of control.
Do the nighttime overeating episodes happen only after you have been trying to restrict your food during the day, or do they also occur on days when you are not dieting or limiting your intake?

I'm not entirely sure, as I haven't tracked my eating closely enough to know if it only happens on days I restrict. I generally just try to eat healthy during the day because of my cardiologist's orders, so it is hard to say.
Do these nighttime overeating episodes happen only after you have been trying to restrict your food during the day, or do they also occur on days when you are not dieting or limiting your intake?

I'm not entirely sure because I don't really keep track of whether it only happens on days I actively try to diet. I just know that this entire cycle of overeating definitely started right after my doctor told me to restrict my food.
Do these overeating episodes happen only after you have been trying to restrict your food intake during the day, or do they also occur on days when you are not dieting or limiting your intake?

I'm not entirely sure about the connection to my day-to-day dieting, but I generally try to eat healthy during the day. What I do know is that the overall urge to overeat definitely started after my cardiologist told me to restrict my food intake.

Do the nighttime overeating episodes happen mainly on days when you have been trying to restrict your food or diet during the day, or do they also happen on days when you have not been limiting yourself?

Yes, they are heavily tied to trying to restrict my food. During the day, I try my best to follow my cardiologist's orders and eat healthy, but the pressure of limiting myself all day—especially on days with medical appointments or when I'm worrying about my heart—just builds up. By nighttime, that tension boiled over and I end up losing control and overeating.

Do these nighttime overeating episodes happen only after you have been trying to restrict your food intake during the day, or do they also happen on days when you have not been dieting or limiting yourself?

I'm not entirely sure about the connection to my daytime dieting specifically. While I am generally supposed to be restricting my food due to my cardiologist's orders, I haven't really paid attention to whether the nighttime episodes only happen on days I strictly dieted versus other days.

When the nighttime eating happens, is it mainly because you feel deprived from restricting food during the day, or does it also happen on nights when you have not been trying to diet or limit yourself?

I'm not entirely sure about the connection between my daytime restriction and these nighttime episodes. Instead of a conscious feeling of daytime deprivation, the urge to eat seems much more tied to the stress of my doctor's appointments, being alone, or worrying about my heart.

When you have these nighttime eating episodes, do they happen mainly after feeling deprived from restricting food during the day, or do they also happen on nights when you are not trying to limit your eating at all?

I'm not quite sure about the connection to daytime restriction versus days when I don't restrict. However, these urges definitely started after my doctor told me to restrict my diet, and they mostly happen when I'm feeling stressed, alone, or after a medical appointment.

Do the nighttime eating episodes happen only after you have been trying to restrict your food intake during the day, or do they also happen on nights when you are not dieting or limiting yourself at all?

I'm not entirely sure if it's directly tied to restricting food during that specific day. However, this overall pattern definitely started after my doctor told me to restrict my diet, and I generally try to eat healthy during the day.

Do you ever have these nighttime overeating episodes on days when you have not been trying to restrict your food or diet during the day, or do they mainly happen after you have been limiting yourself?

I'm not entirely sure about comparing those specific days, because ever since my cardiologist gave me those strict orders, I've been trying to restrict myself almost every single day. Instead, these episodes seem most tied to feeling stressed after my doctor's appointments or when I am left alone at night.

When you have these nighttime eating episodes, do they mainly happen after you have been restricting your food during the day, or do they also happen on nights when you have not been trying to limit your eating?

I'm really not sure if daytime restriction itself is the main trigger. What I do know is that these episodes almost always happen when I am feeling stressed, alone at night, or right after a doctor's appointment where I was reminded to limit my diet.

I'm really not sure, and I haven't really thought about whether I restricted my food on those specific days. I just know that this whole pattern of losing control started after my cardiologist told me to limit my diet.
Do you ever wake up from sleep and eat without being fully aware of it, or are these eating episodes happening while you are awake and conscious at night?

I am completely awake and conscious during these episodes. I usually wander into the kitchen deliberately while I'm working on my handbook or waiting for my wife to go to bed. Even though I feel like I lose control once I start eating, I am fully aware of what I'm doing and I'm definitely not waking up from sleep to do it.
Do you ever eat during the night while half-asleep or after waking from sleep, or are you fully awake and aware each time it happens?

I am fully awake and aware each time it happens. I am usually up late working on my writing or waiting for my wife to go to bed, so I am completely conscious and remember everything. I am definitely not half-asleep or waking up from sleep to do this.
Do you ever wake up from sleep and eat without fully realizing it, or are you always fully awake and aware when the eating happens?

I am always fully awake and aware when this happens, usually because I am up late editing my handbook, worrying, or waiting for my wife to go to sleep. Even though I feel completely out of control and hear myself saying, "Alejandro, basta," I am entirely conscious and awake the entire time.
Do you ever wake up from sleep and eat without being fully aware of it, or are you always fully awake and aware when the eating happens?

I am always fully awake and aware when this happens. It usually occurs late at night while I am up editing my handbook, worrying, or waiting for my wife to go to sleep. I never wake up from sleep to eat.
Do you also eat a lot after waking up during the night or very early in the morning, or is the overeating mainly limited to times when you are awake late at night before going to sleep?

It is definitely limited to the late-night hours before I go to sleep, and I never wake up in the middle of the night or early morning to eat. It always happens while I'm still awake, usually when I am staying up late to edit my handbook, feeling restless, or waiting for my wife to go to bed.
